summary: Design trusted data collaborations, agreements, interoperability profiles, and sustainable operating models. Build practical governance outputs in five days.
lede: Designing trust frameworks and governance for cross-organisation data sharing helps turn policy ambition into accountable, operational collaboration. You will learn to map purpose and authority, classify data, assess consent or lawful basis, define interoperability needs, govern access, and plan incident escalation and value measurement. The course applies ISO/IEC 27001:2022, the NIST Privacy Framework, the W3C Data Catalog Vocabulary, data-sharing agreements, and competition safeguards to practical governance decisions. Through a multi-institution scenario, you will develop a governance charter, agreement issue list, interoperability profile, risk register, KPI dashboard, and phased implementation roadmap.
audienceIntro: Data-sharing governance training is designed for professionals who set rules, negotiate obligations, operate platforms, or fund cross-institution data services. It suits mixed cohorts where legal, policy, technical, and commercial decisions must align.
prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to data governance, privacy, compliance, digital platforms, policy development, or institutional partnership management. No programming is required. Familiarity with contracts, data inventories, APIs, or risk registers will help, but the course introduces the relevant concepts before each exercise.
